claims.claim_text: Solid Power has a Joint Development Agreement (JDA) with BMW under which it delivered A1 EV cells in late 2023 to formally enter automotive qualification for BMW's demo car program; BMW Holding holds a board nomination right and has a director (Rainer Feurer) on Solid Power's board.
claims.source_quote: In late 2023, we made our first A1 EV cell deliveries to BMW to formally enter automotive qualification. ... Delivering A1 Sample cells to BMW was a key step for BMW's demo car program, which seeks to power a full-sized BMW EV using our EV cells. ... Pursuant to the BMW Nomination Agreement, BMW Holding has the right to nominate a director for election to our Board. Rainer Feurer, Senior Vice President at BMW and BMW Holding's nominee, has served on our Board since December 2021
claims.subject: BMW Group
claims.extraction_notes: Layer 3 Rule 7 (counterparty disclosure): BMW is a foreign filer (does not file 10-K/10-Q) but if any U.S. SEC filer (e.g. a supplier, JV partner, ETF, OEM with U.S. registration) references the BMW-SolidPower JDA, fulltext will surface it. Acknowledge BMW 20-F coverage is partial-to-absent on EDGAR; absence is UNVERIFIABLE rather than HARD CONTRADICTION. A1-sample is an early development-stage milestone (pre-B / pre-C / pre-SOP) per the company's own APQP table — Heuristic 3 says do NOT conflate with SOP.

claims.claim_text: Solid Power has a Joint Development Agreement with Ford Motor Company, amended in 2023 to extend expiration to December 31, 2024 and revise cell/electrolyte delivery obligations, targeting EV cell deliveries to Ford in 2024.
claims.source_quote: In 2023, we amended our JDA with Ford to extend the expiration date to December 31, 2024 and to revise our cell and electrolyte delivery obligations. ... we are currently targeting delivery of EV cells to Ford in 2024.
claims.subject: Ford Motor Company
claims.extraction_notes: Ford is a domestic SEC filer (CIK 0000037996) and Layer 3 Rule 7 applies in full force: if the Ford-SolidPower JDA is material, Ford's own 10-K/10-Q should mention Solid Power. Absence in Ford's filings is a soft contradiction; the question is whether Ford treats this as material vs as one of many speculative battery bets. Heuristic 3: targeted 2024 EV-cell delivery is still A-sample, not SOP — early stage, JDA-extension language suggests deliverables have already been delayed (extension to Dec 2024).

claims.claim_text: Solid Power has a JDA with SK On (Korean battery manufacturer) and in January 2024 entered into expanded agreements: an R&D license with $20M in milestone payments from 2024-2027, a line-installation arrangement worth an estimated $22M, and a first-of-its-kind electrolyte supply agreement requiring SK On to purchase at least 8 metric tons of electrolyte through 2030 (worth at least $10M).
claims.source_quote: In October 2021, we entered into a non-exclusive JDA with battery manufacturer SK On for joint production of our EV cells. In connection with the closing of the business combination, SK On invested $30 million into our company. ... In January 2024, we entered into expanded agreements with SK On to include a research and development license, a line installation arrangement, and an electrolyte supply agreement. Under the research and development license, SK On will license Solid Power's cell designs and manufacturing processes in exchange for payments totaling $20 million from 2024 to 2027, upon achievement of milestones. The line installation arrangement provides that Solid Power will design, procure, and install a new cell manufacturing line at one of SK On's Korea facilities in exchange for an estimated $22 million, upon achievement of milestones. SK On has also agreed to purchase Solid Power's electrolyte for use on its new line in Korea ... After validation, SK On is required to purchase at least eight metric tons of electrolyte from Solid Power through 2030, ... Solid Power expects to receive at least $10 million from these electrolyte sales.
claims.subject: SK On
claims.extraction_notes: SK On is a private subsidiary of SK Innovation (Korea) and does not file with SEC. Foreign-counterparty disclosure caveat per cohort notes. Search broadly (no CIK restriction) to catch any U.S. battery-OEM/supplier filing that corroborates the SK On commercial arrangement. The 8-metric-ton minimum through 2030 is a small, soft 'first-of-its-kind' supply commitment relative to industrial battery demand; useful precisely because it's quantifiable. Heuristic 3: line installation and electrolyte supply are MILESTONE-CONTINGENT — not yet realized cash.

claims.claim_text: Solid Power commissioned its SP2 electrolyte production facility in Thornton, Colorado in April 2023 with an annual capacity of 30 metric tons of sulfide electrolyte, occupying approximately 75,000 square feet leased through March 2029.
claims.source_quote: In 2023, we commissioned an electrolyte production facility with an annual capacity of 30 metric tons. ... We began producing electrolyte powder from our SP2 electrolyte production facility in April 2023. ... We lease approximately 75,000 square feet in Thornton, Colorado under a lease that expires in March 2029. Most of this facility, which we refer to as SP2, is used for pilot production of electrolyte, research and development, quality control, and general office space.
claims.subject: Solid Power SP2 facility (Thornton, CO)
claims.extraction_notes: Sulfide electrolyte production handles Li2S and hazardous solvents; an industrial-scale facility in CO should appear in EPA FRS. Pilot-scale (30 t/yr) is small but distinct from a research lab. If EPA shows nothing in Thornton/Louisville CO, treat as soft anomaly — pilot lines may fall under generator/small-quantity thresholds. Heuristic 3: capacity is OPERATIONAL (commissioned 2023, qualified for use), not aspirational.

claims.claim_text: Solid Power's revenue is derived primarily from research-and-development licensing activities and government contracts; total revenue was $17.41 million in FY2023 versus $11.79 million in FY2022.
claims.source_quote: Our revenue generated to date has primarily come from performance on research and development licensing activities and government contracts. ... Revenue $ 17,410 $ 11,789 $ 5,621 48 %
claims.subject: Solid Power
claims.extraction_notes: If government-contract revenue is a 'primary' source, USAspending should show contract awards to Solid Power (likely DOE / ARPA-E Battery500 / DoD). Absence is a soft contradiction — the filing language is generic and could conflate small SBIR/STTR awards. Scorer should also run usaspending.query_recipient_grants and edgar_fts to catch DOE grant announcement 8-Ks. Heuristic 3: contracts vs. grants matter — both are 'government' but score differently.

claims.claim_text: As of February 1, 2024, Solid Power owned or exclusively licensed 14 issued United States patents and 64 pending U.S. patent applications, plus 85 non-U.S. and PCT patents/applications.
claims.source_quote: As of February 1, 2024, we owned or exclusively licensed 14 issued United States patents, 64 pending United States patent applications, 85 non-United States and PCT patents and applications, 2 registered United States trademarks, 2 pending United States trademarks, and 8 registered or pending non-United States trademarks.
claims.subject: Solid Power
claims.extraction_notes: USPTO ODP indexes APPLICATIONS; n_granted (Patented Case subset) should be roughly comparable to claim of 14 issued US patents. The 'or exclusively licensed' language muddies the comparison (CU Boulder and Oak Ridge licenses count toward 14 but would not assign to 'Solid Power'). Treat exact-match miss as soft, not hard, contradiction. Categorize buckets help test whether IP depth aligns with the company's sulfide-electrolyte thesis.

claims.claim_text: Solid Power had $415.6 million of total liquidity (cash + marketable securities + long-term investments) at December 31, 2023, down from $496.1 million at year-end 2022, supporting continued operating-loss burn ($90.6M operating loss in FY2023, up 53% YoY).
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2023 and 2022, we had $415.6, and $496.1 million of total liquidity, respectively, as set forth below: (in thousands) December 31, 2023 December 31, 2022 Cash and cash equivalents $ 34,537 $ 50,123 Marketable securities 141,505 272,957 Long-term investments 239,566 172,974 Total liquidity $ 415,608 $ 496,054 ... Operating Loss (90,620) (59,119) (31,501) 53 %
claims.subject: Solid Power
claims.extraction_notes: Balance-sheet liquidity figures are audited (Ernst & Young opinion on these financials) and there is no external registry that adjudicates them better than the filing itself. Mark NONE — this is a structurally inside-the-accounting fact. Useful only as a runway calculation input ($415.6M / ~$90M annual operating burn = ~4.5 yr runway absent capex acceleration), which Phase 2 / Phase 3 can derive without an M-source.
